Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.

## What looks good

- The whole-program post now refuses a program whose setups differ in End units. `program_problems` compares the End units with the Output and the thread output (`crates/app/src/setup_post_options.rs:89-96`). The refusal names each option that differs (`differing`, line 105). The refusal blocks the post: `post_setup` runs the verification gate, and the test proves the block with `expect_err`.
- The check reads each setup through `of()`: its own options, else the document's. That is the same law `in_force` uses for the posted word, so the check adds no second source for a unit. The document's one program unit (#902, `crate::posting_units`) is untouched.
- The pinning test `setups_disagreeing_on_the_end_units_are_refused_by_name` checks the refusal with each setup active, the message text, a setup that follows the document, agreement, and two differences named together. The older agreement tests still pass, so the change does not refuse a valid program.
- The new code has no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic`. The new function returns names and cannot fail.
- `docs/decisions/1540-end-units-refusal.md` matches the behavior. It keeps the README format, and it names the dropped alternatives.
- The body has a `Changelog:` line and ends `Fixes #1540`. The commit subject follows the convention. The diff changes no process file, golden, snapshot PNG or `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Results, merged with main

Built on the self-hosted pr-test runner: run 43587626231, https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43587626231. The trial merge with main `1bd9298d6b1b5bb2858de6388f9b4d2691023249` was clean.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Quick gate, app suites | Pass, 0 failed, 7.0 min wall |
| `setup_post_options` suite (the Gate map binary) | 11 passed, 0 failed |
| `posting` suite | 17 passed, 0 failed |
| `program_units` suite | 7 passed, 0 failed |
| `tormach_end_units` suite | 7 passed, 0 failed |
| Clippy `-p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` | Clean |

The quick gate planned `setup_post_options` as a whole suite, from the Gate map for `app::setup_post_options` and the changed test file.

## Requested before merge

Nothing.

## Notes (not blocking)

- The refusal names the options in one fixed order: output, threading, end units. Both messages read well.
- The runner checks the Linux arm. The diff adds no `cfg(windows)` line and no per-OS pinned value, so this review owes no local Windows run.
- Not exercised: the review did not run the app, and no posted program ran on a real control. The author states both in the body.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
